slides.title: ContactWorld: What Matters in Vision-Tactile World Models for Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.tldr: VISION-TACTILE WORLD MODELS FOR CONTACT-RICH MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This work explores vision-tactile world models for contact-rich manipulation, demonstrating that spatially structured and temporally continuous multimodal representations improve long-horizon planning. This is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and state modeling.

card.one_liner: ContactWorld shows that spatially structured and temporally continuous representations optimize long-horizon planning in contact-rich robotic manipulation.
card.key_idea: A JEPA-style latent world model using point-cloud observations and tactile force-field (TacFF) representations to preserve geometric relationships and interaction dynamics for MPC-based planning.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 12 tasks (insertion, disassembly, screwing, exploration) using success rates; PointCloud+TacFF achieved the highest average success rate of 36.1%.
card.limitation: Tasks are primarily single-stage and goal-directed; planning performance degrades significantly as prediction horizons increase due to compounding rollout errors.

slides.title: FTP-1: A Generalist Foundation Tactile Policy Across Tactile Sensors for Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.tldr: FOUNDATION TACTILE POLICY FOR CROSS-SENSOR MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: FTP-1 introduces a foundation tactile policy that uses heterogeneous encoders and a shared Transformer to enable tactile skill transfer across diverse sensors and embodiments.

card.one_liner: FTP-1 is a generalist foundation policy enabling transferable tactile manipulation across diverse sensors and robot embodiments.
card.key_idea: Uses Morphology-Aware Tactile Token Space (MTTS) and heterogeneous encoders to project diverse tactile signals into a shared Transformer expert.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 14 contact-rich tasks across 5 hardware setups; showed +17.2% gain on seen sensors and +31% on unseen sensors.
card.limitation: Does not yet address tactile- or force-based servoing and control; pretraining dataset scale and diversity remain limited.

slides.title: Scalable Dynamic Tactile Sensing Enabled by Passive and Flexible Acoustic Waveguides
slides.highlight: This research introduces a passive sensing paradigm using acoustic waveguides that maintains performance during bending, enabling high-resolution tactile localization and waveform reconstruction.

card.one_liner: A scalable, flexible tactile sensing system using passive acoustic waveguides and sparse microphones for real-time localization.
card.key_idea: Interconnected Helmholtz resonators and spring-reinforced microtubes form a waveguide network, using CWT and a lightweight neural network for signal reconstruction and localization.
card.evaluation: Tested via fingertip arrays, gloves, and skins; achieved 4mm resolution and >99% accuracy in a 64-node array; detected 5-mg impacts.

slides.title: GIVE: Grounding Human Gestures in Vision-Language-Action Models
slides.tldr: ENHANCING VLA MODELS WITH HUMAN GESTURE UNDERSTANDING
slides.highlight: GIVE improves human-robot interaction by integrating visual and semantic gesture information into VLA models to resolve ambiguous instructions. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: GIVE enhances VLA models with human gesture understanding using visual-semantic guidance without architectural changes.
card.key_idea: A dual-pathway approach: visual prompting overlays hand skeletons and fingertip rays for spatial grounding, while semantic parsing provides high-level intent descriptions via a VLM.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a Galaxea R1-Lite robot for grasp-and-handover tasks; GIVE improved target recognition by 40% and overall success rate by 80% over baseline.
card.limitation: Performance depends on hand pose estimator accuracy and uses a fixed ray extension scalar, which may fail in extreme depth variations.

slides.title: Impedance MPC with Disturbance Estimation for Dexterous Hand Control
slides.highlight: This framework enables dexterous fingers to track precise trajectories while maintaining safe, compliant contact, supporting the development of embodied social robots in RwB.

card.one_liner: An actuator-agnostic Impedance MPC framework for dexterous hands achieving high precision and zero steady-state error under contact.
card.key_idea: Combines algebraic feedforward reduction to a double integrator with a 500Hz receding-horizon QP and an encoder-only Kalman disturbance estimator.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a hydraulic finger and 16-DOF LEAP Hand simulation; outperformed classical impedance with 0.1 mrad steady-state error under 1.5 Nm load.
card.limitation: The quasi-static pressure map fails during stiff, fast rigid impacts that excite compressibility modes, requiring an augmented-pressure-state model.

slides.title: World Pilot: Steering Vision-Language-Action Models with World-Action Priors
slides.tldr: VLA MODELS AUGMENTED WITH WORLD-ACTION PRIORS
slides.highlight: World Pilot introduces a framework that uses scene-evolution and trajectory priors to improve VLA model performance in contact-rich manipulation tasks. This is relevant to MOSAIC's focus on aligning human-AI intent and improving skill acquisition through adaptive motion and perception priors.

card.one_liner: World Pilot enhances VLA models using world-action priors to improve robustness against out-of-distribution manipulation shifts.
card.key_idea: It uses Latent Steering to inject scene-evolution latents into VLM hidden states and Action Steering to provide trajectory-level motion priors to the action generator.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on LIBERO-Plus (84.7% success), RoboCasa, and real-robot tasks. Results show state-of-the-art OOD robustness, particularly under viewpoint and geometry shifts.
card.limitation: Performance degrades when scenes fall outside the WAM's pretraining distribution and per-step WAM forward passes limit high-frequency reactive control.

slides.title: Elastic Queries Reinforcement Learning: Self-Aware Policy Execution for VLA Models
slides.tldr: ADAPTIVE INFERENCE SCHEDULING FOR VLA MODELS
slides.highlight: EQRL introduces a framework that dynamically adjusts denoising budgets and action chunk lengths based on state difficulty to reduce inference costs in VLA models.

card.one_liner: EQRL adaptively adjusts VLA inference budget and action chunk length to reduce compute cost without sacrificing success.
card.key_idea: A lightweight RL adaptor jointly optimizes latent steering, denoising steps, and chunk length, using critic-ensemble disagreement to allocate more compute to difficult states.
card.evaluation: Tested on LIBERO and ALOHA simulations and real robots; EQRL reduced relative NFE by 20-24% while preserving or improving task success.
card.limitation: Offline training lacks causal feedback for different schedules, and the adaptor currently requires per-task fine-tuning with limited cross-task generalization.

slides.title: PhysVLA: Towards Physically-Grounded VLA for Embodied Robotic Manipulation
slides.tldr: PHYSICS-GROUNDED VLA FRAMEWORK FOR ROBOTIC MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: PhysVLA introduces a plug-and-play framework that enforces physical principles on VLA models to improve success rates and trajectory stability. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction through enhanced robotic control.

card.one_liner: PhysVLA is a training-free, plug-and-play framework that adds physical grounding to frozen VLA models during inference.
card.key_idea: A dual-layered corrector using a phase-aware finite-state machine for task segments and a selective Euler-Lagrange gate to rectify kinodynamically inconsistent actions.
card.evaluation: Tested on LIBERO-Spatial and Robosuite with four VLA backbones; showed up to 17% success increase and 10x jerk robustness improvement.
card.limitation: Depends on accurate URDF/XML robot calibration and cannot fully resolve tasks requiring sub-centimetre precision due to the 5% correction cap.
